note: Positive and defeating cases for contracts/authority-grant.schema.json and the evaluator in scripts/sovkernel/authority.py. Three cases prove a live grant covers a request; thirty-three prove a refusal, and every refusal code the evaluator can report has at least one case proving it actually fires. Each case is a patch over base_grant and base_request, so what a case says is exactly what it changes; a field a case does not mention is the base value, and a field neither mentions is absent rather than satisfied.

cases.proves: The whole point of the standing grant: a change inside scope, on an admitted branch, under budget, with a green verify and lint and an independent CONFIRMED observation, lands without a fresh conversation.
A ceiling admits every class at or below it. A RECORD_LOCAL commit is covered by a RESOURCE_CONSUMPTION grant; the ceiling is a maximum, not an equality.
Writing a grant is not the same act as switching it on. A grant at PROPOSED standing is inert, so a participant cannot author its own authority into effect.
A grant is exercised by the actor it names and by nobody else.
Scope is per capability. A grant that can land cannot thereby ratify; the capability list is exhaustive.
Revocation refuses visibly (SPEC.md, PROD-I-5), and refuses on its own without waiting for the expiry.
A grant issued for a future window does not reach backwards.
A standing grant that never has to be renewed stops being a decision. Past valid_until it refuses, and nothing in the loop can extend it.
An exclusion beats an inclusion. decisions/ sits under no included prefix and is excluded besides, so the loop cannot record its own policy.
The registry sits under contracts/, which the grant otherwise admits. Excluding it by name is what stops an exercise of the grant from widening the grant it is being exercised under.

scripts/../STATUS.yaml begins with an admitted prefix and names an excluded file. Found live on main on 2026-08-25, with the grant ratified, by a witness that had already dissented once. A prefix comparison cannot see through a `..` segment, so the evaluator refuses the spelling rather than pretending to grade it.

The same escape aimed at the one exclusion that exists to stop an exercise of the grant widening the grant. D-008a proves the plain spelling is refused; this proves the traversal spelling is too, which is the pair that makes the exclusion mean something.

A traversal that climbs past the repository root reaches a file no scope prefix describes at all. The evaluator holds no root and cannot tell where it landed, which is exactly why it refuses the spelling instead of resolving it.

contracts/./standing-grants.json does not begin with the excluded string and is the excluded file; git add stages the real registry. Found by a witness on 2026-08-25 against a version of this evaluator that refused `..` and absolute paths and nothing else, which is why the predicate is now a property rather than a list of known escapes.

The same escape spelled with an empty segment instead of a dot. It is the pair with D-008f: two different spellings of one file, both admitted by a prefix comparison, both resolved by git. A path is gradeable only when every segment names something.
A request path names a file, so a trailing separator leaves an empty final segment and the string stops describing one thing. Refused by the same property, without a rule of its own.

contracts/* is inside an admitted prefix and is not the excluded string, and git add stages the excluded registry with it. A pattern names no file until git expands it, which happens after the scope check has already decided. Found by a witness on 2026-08-25 against a version of this evaluator that had closed every normalisation escape and none of the globbing ones.

contracts/standing-grants.jso? differs from the excluded string by one character and selects it. A fix that stripped only `*` would leave this open, which is why the pair is here: the class is pattern characters, not the asterisk.
contracts/[s]tanding-grants.json is the third spelling of one escape. Three cases rather than one because each was reachable on its own against a fix aimed at the others.

A leading colon opens git's pathspec magic, which changes what a string selects before matching begins. No magic spelling was found that both passed the evaluator and staged an excluded file, so this closes a reachable class rather than a demonstrated escape; refusing it costs nothing, because no repository path begins with a colon.

contracts is repository-relative, carries no pattern character and no non-naming segment, and git add -- contracts stages the grant registry and the grant schema. It is the one escape class that cannot be seen in the string, which is why the exclusion check asks in both directions: not whether the path begins with an excluded prefix, but whether it selects something excluded. Found by a witness on 2026-08-25 against a version that had closed every string-level class.

The depth control for D-008m. contracts/sub is a directory too, and nothing excluded lives under it, so it stays admitted. A fix that refused directories outright rather than asking what they contain would fail here, which is the difference between closing the escape and closing the gate.

A grant declares repository-relative prefixes, so an absolute path is not comparable to one. The first sov-loop run fed exactly this and it was refused for the wrong reason - no prefix matched - which reads identically to a grant refusing the file. Naming the real reason is what tells a caller to normalise rather than to ask for a wider grant.
Scope is an allow list, not a deny list. A path nobody thought to exclude is still outside the grant unless a prefix admits it.
The branches a grant names are the branches it reaches. A grant to land on main is not a grant to land anywhere.
An over-budget grant refuses visibly (SPEC.md, PROD-I-5). A run that sprawled past its envelope stops at the landing gate rather than at nothing.
A RECORD_LOCAL grant does not stretch to cover resource consumption merely because the work is otherwise in scope.
JUDGEMENT authority may be issued by the owner alone. A participant that writes itself a judgement grant has written nothing.
Phase FOUNDING admits no external-world effect, and the phase refuses before any grant is consulted. No grant can be written that gets around it.
A build cannot witness itself. A landing request carrying only its own green checks is a self-report, and the gate says so.
An observation that exists but does not confirm is not an observation the gate can stand on. Only CONFIRMED counts.
A helper that read or edited the change is inside the build and can never witness it (AGENTS.md, Closure ownership). The gate refuses the substitution rather than trusting the label.
A check the request does not mention is absent, never satisfied. Silence is not a pass.
main stays releasable. A failing repository check stops the landing at the gate, not at review.

A backslash is a path separator on Windows and an ordinary legal filename character on POSIX, so one string names two different files depending on where the check runs, and this module reads no host. Normalising it to `/` before comparing is safe in one direction only: it over-refuses an excluded path, which is harmless, and over-admits an included one, which is not. On POSIX a root-level file literally named scripts\tests\x.py normalised to scripts/tests/x.py and was admitted under the prefix scripts/ while sitting nowhere near it. Reached from two Linux CI failures on a Windows-only assertion, reported by a sibling session.

The refusal is on the character, not on where it sits. A path whose leading segment is admitted and whose tail carries a backslash still names one file on one host and another elsewhere. A caller canonicalises first with sovland.tree.repo_relative; one that does not gets the refusal.
